audit: Second exhaustive audit: evidence, calculations, reporting, experiments

confirmed_findings.title: Markdown export turns untrusted evidence into active image/HTML markup
confirmed_findings.description: report_markdown places exact uploaded/retrieved source text directly in a Markdown blockquote without escaping Markdown syntax or HTML. Prefixing a line with '> ' does not disable images or HTML. A supplier attachment containing ![supplier tracking pixel](https://tracking.invalid/supplier-pixel) and passes upload, preflight, the full simulated worker pipeline, saved-report validation, and export; the downloaded ready Markdown retains both as active markup. Titles, option labels and model summaries have the same interpolation problem. An image-capable Markdown preview can therefore fetch an attacker-selected remote image merely when the exported report is viewed; HTML-capable viewers additionally receive raw HTML. This is an export rendering-policy defect, not a claim that the application itself executed the image or script.
confirmed_findings.expected_behavior: Escape untrusted text into inert Markdown literals (or render it with a consistent allowlisted policy), preserve exact bytes separately if needed, and prohibit remote images/raw HTML in report rendering.

repository_contract.requirement: RPT-04 requires no arbitrary HTML or remote image/tracking loads, and explicitly says browser and export paths enforce the same renderer policy.

proof.observed: HTTP meeting create 201; text upload ready; preflight blockers []; start 202; real simulated worker drain completed; Markdown export ready; download 200; four raw external image expressions retained, including two from uploaded supplier evidence.
proof.network_scope: No external request or paid call was made. tracking.invalid is a synthetic inert destination.

limitations_not_counted_as_confirmed_bug.title: No production path currently makes cost evidence supported, so real ready_to_choose is unreachable
limitations_not_counted_as_confirmed_bug.evidence: Every original cost component source_ref is rewritten to newly created structured evidence with verification_status=user_supplied. The cost dependency accepts only supported sources. The probe exercises real evidence preparation and real supported-claim persistence, then ideal positive distinct-provider review records: positive included costs and explicit included zero costs both pass all hard requirements yet remain conditional solely due to the unverified cost dependency. Excluded and not-applicable-only cases also remain conditional with their expected additional cost gaps. All four probes accept a supported fact claim without promoting source verification. No runtime evidence-verification mutation route was found.
limitations_not_counted_as_confirmed_bug.why_not_a_confirmed_defect: Repository documentation consistently says entered costs are not independently verified and readiness requires accepted scoped support; it does not clearly promise that current functionality must let a user promote those sources. Treat this as a product capability limitation until an explicit supported-evidence acceptance workflow is required, rather than weakening the conservative readiness gate.
